name: PROTOCOL AI NAVY SEAL
scope: All1203lines fully read, including two spawned near-duplicate controllers. Truncated observations were followed by bounded rereads. Binary startup/dependencies/licence unverified.
intent: Shoreline approach, passenger disembarkation and dry-ground movement, then supporting/assault elements and casualty protection.
existingCbe: CortexGroupTick -> CortexNavalAssault -> CortexNavalRelease. Bounded shore comparison and finite native approach; separate passenger group and combined-group egress cases, operating crew retained, token/expiry/speed receipts. Ground combat continues through common finite infantry controllers.
sourceDefects: Two independent spawned workers share naval flags and actors; no locality/Zeus/native/new-operation ownership.
First shallow test depth>=0.1 AND<=0.1 accepts only exact0.1m; second duplicate uses0.09..0.11m. Repeated nested shoreline queries remain narrow and potentially fail.
Approach waits until boat death/disembark condition without absolute abort; inner infantry loop lasts while any original actor alive and can block other groups indefinitely.
Global allUnits hostile oracle and live transforms, side inequality; no authored-waypoint use despite _hasWaypoint variable.
Repeated moveOut/unassignVehicle and lockCargo true override crew/cargo intent; leader selection and RED/COMBAT/FULL/WEDGE overrides have no restoration.
Second duplicate creates smoke inventory before forced fire; repeated selectBestPlaces peractor without route/physical arrival authority.
Land-return helper is defined but unused; no meaningful finite natural handover after threat loss.
remaining: Actual shore/nav path quality, mixed cargo/crew locality, refusal/repeat/migration, landing-to-ground combat and performance need physical evidence. Do not call source duplication two separate desired features.
sourceProtection: Original PBO and extracted readable files verified against inventory hashes; no raw source copied into product.
validation: Source review, caller tracing, JSON parsing and archive/extract hash verification. No product edit or runtime test in this batch.

confirmedPaths: CortexGroupTick calls CortexNavalAssault before state selection, then later CortexVehicles and CortexTacticalStart. The mounted native group leader remains the generic brain leader.

CortexTacticalAssess computes _hasCrew from actual driver/gunner/commander seats and returns VEHICLE_DOMAIN whenever operating crew coexist with infantry. This is an intentional defence against group destinations moving vehicles onto land, not missing native enemy knowledge.

CortexAssaultStart already builds _onFoot and separate assault/cover elements, creates no group waypoint and passes explicit participants/pairElements to OperationStart. CortexFlankStart separately refuses mounted group anchors.

CortexFlankStep uses CortexGroupAnchor in recovery/rally paths; that helper prefers an eligible native group leader. CortexFlankEnd also retains formation handback semantics. Reusing assault admission alone would leave boat-based recovery/handback.

OperationStep already tracks participantProgress separately and only uses leader fallback when participantsRequired is false. Changing its generic progress anchor alone would not resolve the tactical domain gate or recovery anchor.
groundCommandTrace20261023.nextImplementation: Provide an explicit admitted ground-element context through existing tactical assessment, actor manoeuvre and recovery/cleanup. Keep vessel crew outside that element, preserve the original group/native mission route and new-order authority, and use a living current element member for rally/casualty succession. Do not remove the blanket mixed-group gate globally or redirect CortexGroupAnchor for unrelated operations. Avoid a duplicate permanent controller or unconditional native selectLeader/group split.
groundCommandTrace20261023.limits: This trace narrows the required implementation. No runtime code changed, no parity credit, no physical acceptance and no extra full build of unchanged runtime.

elementAnchorImplementation20261023.scope: Participant-local anchor foundation; not independent mixed-group tactical admission.
elementAnchorImplementation20261023.implementation: CortexGroupAnchor optional explicit element selects only current local combat-effective on-foot group members from at most64 supplied actors. Explicit empty/unavailable rosters return objNull; native group leader can win only when in the supplied element. Default callers retain fast leader path and12-member fallback. CortexAssaultStart uses _onFoot; CortexFlankStep recovery uses surviving _main and defers on missing witness, retaining existing buddy/nearest-peer preference. No selectLeader, join or new controller.
elementAnchorImplementation20261023.remaining: TacticalAssess mixed-crew VEHICLE_DOMAIN gate and full admitted ground-element context/cleanup remain unresolved; do not globally bypass them. Ordinary final formation handback remains native group semantics, not independent naval ground command.

landedElementCloseAssault20261023.implementation: Successful same-group egress captures at most64 original cargo actors into a semantic handover using the existing45-second LANDED expiry. Owner epoch, boat plan token/group/phase and unchanged native route bind admission. Existing group job dispatches existing TacticalStart/Assess/AssaultStart with an explicit foot roster; native believed contact distances are measured from its foot anchor. Only close ASSAULT may pass; group flank/advance/reposition and fallback remain forbidden for this context. No new worker, FSM, native leader change or group split.
landedElementCloseAssault20261023.lifecycle: Accepted assault consumes pending context and uses its ordinary finite operation/FSM. Original foot roster bounds casualty refill. Existing participant-local recovery anchors apply; scoped final follow requests target a surviving member rather than mounted group leader. Ordinary squad self-follow formation reset remains unchanged. Feature closure, takeover, changed native route/epoch or expiry retire pending context; generic CortexReleaseGroup now includes it even after naval operation retirement.
landedElementCloseAssault20261023.sourceIntent: Progress toward a ground element that continues fighting after landing while operating crew stay aboard. Deliberately replaces unowned source selectLeader/RED/FULL/WEDGE and repeated force-exit loops with existing actor executor and ownership boundaries.
landedElementCloseAssault20261023.remaining: Close-assault handover only. General independent long-range advance, CQB/urban continuation and durable ground command are not implemented by this change. Native subformation/follow acknowledgement, leader-anchor stopping/continuation, waves, casualties, refusal, owner changes, Zeus interruption and physical authored-order handback require in-engine observation. Do not count command issue as physical acceptance or declare naval parity.
